title: The five characteristics of a project
blurb: Name the five characteristics that set project work apart from business as usual, and spot each one in a situation.
question: A housing association has refurbished kitchens many times, but this time the contractor, the estate and the timescale are all new. Which characteristic of a project does this illustrate?

teach.body: PRINCE2 names five characteristics that distinguish project work from business as usual: change, temporary, cross-functional, unique and uncertainty. Business as usual repeats familiar work with settled teams. A project brings people together for a while to introduce something new, so it is harder to plan, harder to coordinate and riskier. Knowing the five tells you why projects need a structured method.

teach.caption: The last one is the result of the first four.

teach.h: How the first four create uncertainty
teach.caption: Because of the other four, projects are riskier than business as usual.

teach.h: Why this makes projects harder to manage
teach.body: Routine work improves through repetition. A project rarely gets that chance: its team is new, its mix of skills crosses departmental lines, and its circumstances have not been met in exactly this form before. The change it introduces also affects people outside the team. So a project needs explicit roles, plans, controls and risk management that business as usual can take for granted.

teach.h: Unique vs temporary: the classic mix-up

rows.label: Clue
values: Ends when change is in place

teach.body: Ashdown Homes, a housing association, is replacing heating in 200 homes. Project manager Tomasz Nowak notes the five characteristics. Change: tenants move to heat pumps. Temporary: the project closes once the systems are handed over to the maintenance team. Cross-functional: engineers, tenant liaison staff and finance work together. Unique: earlier heating projects used a different contractor and ran in summer. Uncertainty: supply delays could hurt, while a grant could help.

teach.h: Which characteristic is the question describing?

teach.text: A different team, customer, supplier, location or timeframe points to UNIQUE, even when the organization has run similar projects before. TEMPORARY is about the project ending once its change is in place. And uncertainty covers opportunities as well as threats.

items: Five characteristics: change, temporary, cross-functional, unique, uncertainty (1.3).
Change: projects are the means of introducing change.
Temporary: once the change is in place, business as usual resumes in its new form.
Cross-functional: people with different skills work together temporarily on a change that affects others.
Unique: every project differs in some way. Uncertainty: the other four add threats and opportunities, so projects are riskier.

summary: You can now name the five characteristics of a project and explain each one. You can also recognize which characteristic a situation illustrates, including telling unique apart from temporary.

A.q: Which is one of the five characteristics that distinguish project work from business as usual?
A.why: Cross-functional is one of the five characteristics (change, temporary, cross-functional, unique, uncertainty).

whyNot.0: Focus on products is a PRINCE2 principle, not one of the characteristics of a project.
whyNot.1: Fixed pricing is a possible commercial arrangement, not a characteristic of project work.
whyNot.3: Manage by exception is a PRINCE2 principle, not one of the characteristics of a project.

A.q: A transport authority has upgraded several bus stations using the same approach. The next upgrade has a different contractor, a different town and a winter timeframe. Which characteristic does this illustrate?
A.why: Every project is unique: even when similar projects have been done, each differs in some way, such as team, supplier, location or timeframe.

whyNot.0: Temporary is about the project ending once its change is in place, not how it differs from earlier projects.
whyNot.2: Change is about projects being the means of introducing change, not about differences from earlier work.
whyNot.3: Uncertainty is the extra threats and opportunities that result; the clue here is the differences themselves.

A.q: Which characteristic describes people with different skills working together for a while on a change that affects others outside the team?
A.why: Cross-functional means a team of people with different skills working together temporarily to introduce a change that will affect others outside the team.

whyNot.1: Temporary describes the project's lifespan, not the mix of skills.
whyNot.2: Change describes what projects are for, not who works on them.
whyNot.3: Unique describes how each project differs from others, not the make-up of the team.

B.q: Identify the missing word in the following sentence. Projects are the means by which an organization introduces [?].
B.why: The change characteristic: projects are the means by which change is introduced.

whyNot.0: Governance is how a project is directed and controlled; projects are not described as the means of introducing it.
whyNot.1: Tolerance is the permitted deviation from a plan, used in manage by exception.
whyNot.2: Assurance checks that a project is being run properly; it is not what projects exist to introduce.

B.q: Why does PRINCE2 say projects are riskier than business as usual?
options: They are funded from capital budgets instead of operating budgets
Their other characteristics bring threats and opportunities beyond routine work
They are staffed with less experienced people than the teams who run daily operations
They are directed by a project board instead of by line managers
B.why: The uncertainty characteristic: change, temporary, cross-functional and unique together introduce threats and opportunities over and above those of business as usual.

whyNot.0: How a project is funded is not the reason PRINCE2 gives for projects being riskier.
whyNot.2: PRINCE2 does not say project staff are less experienced; the risk comes from the nature of project work.
whyNot.3: A project board is part of how projects are governed, not the cause of their extra risk.

B.q: According to the temporary characteristic, when does the need for a project end?
options: When the supplier's contract reaches its renewal date
When the project manager's annual appointment expires
When the change is in place and business as usual resumes
When the first product is handed over to the users
B.why: Once the desired change has been implemented, business as usual resumes in its new form and the need for the project is removed.

whyNot.0: A contract date is a commercial matter; the project ends when its change is in place.
whyNot.1: Appointments do not decide a project's lifespan; the completed change does.
whyNot.3: Handing over one product may happen before the whole change is in place, so the project may still be needed.

C.q:
Which two statements about the characteristics of a project are correct?
1. Uncertainty means projects bring opportunities as well as threats.
2. Unique means the organization has not run any similar project before.
3. A cross-functional team introduces a change that affects people outside the team.
4. Temporary means a project must be completed within a single stage.
C.why: Statement 1 is right: uncertainty introduces threats and opportunities. Statement 3 is right: cross-functional teams introduce a change that affects others outside the team.

whyNot.0: Statement 2 is false: an organization may run many similar projects, yet each still differs in some way.
whyNot.2: Statements 2 and 4 are false. A PRINCE2 project has at least two stages, so it is not limited to a single stage.
whyNot.3: Statement 4 is false: temporary means the project ends once its change is in place; PRINCE2 projects have at least two stages.

C.q: A retailer has opened twelve stores using the same plan. The thirteenth is in a new country with a new landlord, and exchange rate movements could raise or lower its costs. Which characteristics are shown by the new country and landlord, and by the exchange rate effect?
C.why: New location and landlord make this store project unique despite the proven plan. Exchange rates that could help or hurt are threats and opportunities: uncertainty.

whyNot.1: Neither clue is about the project ending (temporary) or about projects introducing change.
whyNot.2: The first clue is unique, but costs that could rise or fall show uncertainty, not change.
whyNot.3: The exchange rate effect is uncertainty, but a new country and landlord show uniqueness, not a mix of skills.

C.q: Which characteristic explains why a project's team disbands at the end, and what carries on afterwards?
options: Change; a follow-on project embeds the new way of working
Unique; a standard routine replaces the project's own methods
Uncertainty; the risk register passes to the operations team
Temporary; business as usual resumes in its new form
C.why: Projects are temporary: once the change is implemented, business as usual resumes in its new form and the need for the project, and its team, is removed.

whyNot.0: Change explains why projects exist, not why they end, and PRINCE2 does not require a follow-on project.
whyNot.1: Unique is about each project differing from others, not about the project ending.
whyNot.2: Uncertainty is about extra threats and opportunities, not about the project ending.

reteach.title: Think of a wedding
reteach.question: A couple plans a wedding: caterers, a florist, a photographer and a venue team come together for one day, and then go their separate ways. Where are the five characteristics?

blocks.body: The wedding changes the couple's lives (change). The suppliers work together for a short time and then disband (temporary). Caterer, florist and photographer bring different skills, and guests are affected (cross-functional). Even a venue that hosts weddings every week has never hosted this couple, this guest list and this date (unique). So there are extra threats, such as rain, and opportunities, such as a late discount (uncertainty).

blocks.text: The venue's weekly routine of hosting weddings is business as usual for the venue. Each individual wedding is still unique.

explain.body: Projects are the means by which an organization introduces change. They are temporary: when the change is in place, business as usual resumes in its new form and the project is no longer needed.

test.q: A council wants all its staff to move from paper timesheets to a new online system. Which characteristic of a project does this aim best show?
test.why: Moving staff to a new way of working is introducing change, and projects are the means by which change is introduced.

whyNot.0: Nothing in the aim says how this project differs from others.
whyNot.2: The aim says nothing about a mix of skills working together.
whyNot.3: The aim does not describe threats or opportunities.

explain.body: A project brings together people with different skills, often from different departments or organizations, on a temporary basis. The change they introduce affects others outside the team, so coordination and communication matter.

test.q: A six-month project team brings together a structural engineer, a trainer, a buyer and a tenant liaison officer. Which characteristic does the mix of skills best show?
test.why: People with different skills working together temporarily on a change is the cross-functional characteristic.

whyNot.0: The six months hints at temporary, but the question asks about the mix of skills.
whyNot.1: Unique is about how the project differs from others, not the mix of skills.
whyNot.3: Change is about what projects introduce, not who is on the team.

explain.body: Every project is unique. An organization may run many similar projects with a proven pattern, but each one differs in some way: a different team, customer, supplier, location or timeframe.

test.q: An organization has run many similar projects with a proven pattern. What does PRINCE2 say about the next one?
options: It can be run as business as usual using the same plan
It is no longer a project once the pattern is proven
It needs no business case because the pattern is proven
It will still differ in some way, so it is still unique
test.why: Even with a familiar pattern, each project differs in some way (team, customer, supplier, location or timeframe), so every project is unique.

whyNot.0: A familiar pattern helps, but the project is still a project with its own differences, not business as usual.
whyNot.1: A proven pattern does not stop work being a project; it still introduces change and is temporary.
whyNot.2: Every project needs an agreed business case, however familiar the pattern.

explain.body: Change, temporary, cross-functional and unique together introduce threats and opportunities over and above those of business as usual. Projects are riskier, which is why PRINCE2 has a risk practice and controls such as stages and tolerances.

test.q: What does the uncertainty characteristic add to project work?
options: Threats and opportunities beyond those of business as usual
Threats that the business layer must accept before initiation
Opportunities that the supplier must exploit for the customer
Costs that must be held in a contingency outside the budget
test.why: The characteristics of projects introduce threats and opportunities over and above those typically met in business as usual, so projects are riskier.

whyNot.1: PRINCE2 does not say the business layer must accept all threats before initiation; risks are managed throughout.
whyNot.2: Uncertainty is not defined as opportunities a supplier must exploit; it covers threats and opportunities alike.
whyNot.3: Budgets for risk responses are covered by the risk practice; this is not what the characteristic means.
